title: jmap-server: HandlerFuture supports multiple response invocations
description:
Modify jmap-server so a single handler call can produce multiple entries in methodResponses. Required for RFC 8621 §7.5 EmailSubmission/set onSuccessUpdateEmail, which MUST append an implicit Email/set invocation after the submission response.

## Exact change

### src/lib.rs — change HandlerFuture return type

Old:
```rust
pub type HandlerFuture = Pin<Box<dyn Future<Output = Result<Value, JmapError>> + Send>>;
```

New:
```rust
/// The primary response value plus any additional invocations to append to methodResponses.
/// Most handlers return Ok((value, vec![])).
/// EmailSubmission/set with onSuccessUpdateEmail returns Ok((subm_value, vec![(Email/set, email_value, call_id)])).
pub type HandlerFuture = Pin<Box<dyn Future<Output = Result<(Value, Vec<Invocation>), JmapError>> + Send>>;
```

### src/lib.rs — update dispatch() loop

Existing dispatch code creates  invocation.
Change to:
```rust
// After awaiting the spawned handler task:
let (primary_value, extra_invocations) = ok_result;
method_responses.push((method.clone(), primary_value, call_id.clone()));
method_responses.extend(extra_invocations);
```

## Acceptance criteria
- cargo test -p jmap-server passes
- cargo clippy -p jmap-server -- -D warnings passes
- RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc -p jmap-server --no-deps passes
- The public JmapHandler trait now requires handlers to return (Value, Vec<Invocation>)
- Existing single-invocation tests still pass (returns empty Vec as second element)
- New test: handler returns two invocations → both appear in JmapResponse::method_responses in order

## Defensive programming rules
- The dispatcher MUST push the primary response BEFORE extending with extra invocations
- extra_invocations MUST be appended in the order returned by the handler (no reordering)
- No unwrap/expect added
- jmap-server is a locked crate — this is an explicitly authorized targeted change
